purpose: Illustrative academic workbench scene, not an actual ICTRA prototype photograph or experimental evidence.
prompt: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Asset type: editorial hero photograph for a student biosignal research website. Create one photorealistic, unglamorous close-up of a modest university electronics workbench in soft daylight. A small blue microcontroller development board and a small green signal acquisition breakout rest on a slightly worn light oak desk, with three loose white circular adhesive snap electrodes and their gray leads, colored green, yellow, and red snap connectors. Electrodes are lying on the table, NOT attached to a person. A silver laptop corner and a paper notebook are partially visible and softly out of focus in the back; no screen contents or readable text. Observational documentary photography, 50mm lens, gentle depth of field, naturally irregular cable curves, plausible solder joints and pin headers, real paper fibers, fine wood grain, restrained neutral colors, slight everyday imperfections. Landscape 3:2 composition; hardware and electrode pads are the clear subjects, framed with breathing room. Honest quiet academic atmosphere, not a glossy advertising product render. No people, no hands, no holograms, no floating waveforms, no brain illustrations, no neon light, no sci-fi, no glowing traces, no fake dashboard, no text overlays, no labels, no logo, no watermark. This is a conceptual research scene, not a claimed photograph of a specific real prototype.
